bull.b: Minimal debt reduces interest and refinancing pressure, preserving flexibility while the company advances its oncology programs. This gives management more capacity to direct available resources toward research, partnering, and development rather than servicing a material debt burden.

Preclinical activity in lung, head and neck, and bladder cancer specimens resistant to prior immunotherapy supports the platform’s scientific potential. Reduced cytokine responses and longer half-life in primates may improve the therapeutic profile and development prospects.

Granted U.S. protection around CAPTN-3 constructs and methods of use can help defend the company’s technology and improve its negotiating position with potential partners. A stronger IP estate may support continued platform development and commercialization opportunities.

bear.b: The absence of meaningful revenue means the business remains dependent on funding or partnering to support operations. Persistent large operating and net losses indicate that the pipeline has not yet produced commercial earnings, limiting evidence of a self-sustaining business model.

Continued negative operating and free cash flow consumes financial resources while the company advances its pipeline. Although burn improved from 2024, it worsened versus 2025, showing that cash usage remains material and could constrain development or require additional financing.

The substantial multi-year reduction in equity reflects the cumulative impact of ongoing losses and leaves a smaller capital base to support future research and development. This weakens financial flexibility and makes continued execution more dependent on successful funding or partnerships.
